newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas commented on news reports on flexibility and repeated the comments he made on Thursday (see Thursday's BC-COMMISSION-BRIEFING). He also said that EMU did not necessarily require deep taxation and social harmonisation.
Van der Pas rejected the thesis that taxation harmonisation could be imposed through flexibility on a reluctant member state and therefore create a new criterion for monetary union.

Spokesmen Joao Vale de Almeida briefed on Monday and Tuesday's General Affairs Council. He said the agenda would include the political situation in the Great Lakes region and forthcoming elections in Zaire.
Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said the foreign ministers would also discuss Yugoslav issues such as the situation in Belgrade, local elections in Croatia and March's international donors conference.

Wegter said the agenda would also include the proposal for an EU fact-finding mission in Belarus. He said the Commission had decided to suspend the second part of 1995 funding to Belarus until good use of the 25 Mecus could be proved.

Spokesman Josep Coll i Cabro said some Common Foreign and Security Policy issues such as the Middle East peace process would be discussed in select committee. He said the agenda would also include preparation of the EU-ASEAN and the EU-ASEM Ministerial meetings in Singapore, Mediterranean policy and trade questions such as transatlantic relations after the WTO ministerial conference in Singapore and WTO negotiations on basic telecommunications.

Spokesman Willy Helin said Commissioner Karel Van Miert had made comments on the British Airways/American Airlines dispute in answer to British Prime Minister John Major's statement in the House of Commons on Thursday.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/19: Cross-border transfers: Commissioner Monti welcomes definitive adoption of directive.
- IP/97/20: Infringement: Belgium fails to comply with the rules governing excise duties on non-alcoholic beverages.
- IP/97/21: Infringements: Incorrect application of the Sixth VAT Directive by Italy, France, Germany and Austria.
- IP/97/22: Infringements: Italy - recycling charge on polyethylene and plastic film.
- IP/97/23: European Commission confirms commitment in new areas of support for the New Independent States: justice and home affairs; and WTO accession.
- IP/97/24: British Airways - American Airlines: "I hope we will find a solution that completely satisfies European competition worries", says Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
- Speech/97/7: Speech by Commissioner Christos Papoutsis on "travel and tourism employment: a European view".
- Speech/97/8: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler at opening for International Green Week 1997 in Berlin.
- Eurostat news release No 3/97: EU unemployment: 10.9% in November.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1996-40: Only hesitant upturn in industry.
- Eurostat Energy monthly statistics No 1996-11.
- ME97/17.1: Midday Express.
